key_insight: Long-term gantenerumab treatment substantially lowered brain amyloid-β proteoforms in postmortem tissue from dominantly inherited Alzheimer disease, while solanezumab showed little measurable effect.
clinical_relevance: These results support postmortem biochemical readouts as a useful way to confirm target engagement and compare how anti-amyloid antibodies reshape brain pathology.
method: High-resolution mass spectrometry on postmortem brain homogenates
Quantified amyloid-β and tau proteoforms in soluble and insoluble fractions
Compared treated DIAD cases with untreated DIAD carriers and non-DIAD controls
evidence_signal: In the abstract, gantenerumab was associated with about 60–80% lower insoluble Aβ42/Aβ40 and reduced modified Aβ3pGlu, plus lower phosphorylated and MTBR tau species, whereas solanezumab showed no significant overall proteoform changes.
watch_item: The treated groups were very small (n=4 per antibody), so the findings are informative but need larger studies before broad generalization.
paper_title: Gantenerumab reduces brain amyloid-β proteoforms: Biochemical evaluation in dominantly inherited Alzheimer disease
